title: The Foundation Beneath the Twelve Storeys

features.name: the-root-deep
features.desc-on-touch: Roots run through the foundation like the building learned to grow downward. They don't support—they question. The twelve storeys above shift constantly; the roots below never change.

features.name: the-stairwell-that-descends-too-far
features.desc-on-touch: Stairs spiral down through the foundation. Each step is from a different apartment, a different year, a different version of the building that was never permanent enough to exist.

features.name: the-resident-lists-converge
features.desc-on-touch: Names carved into the concrete. Each layer of names contradicts the layer beneath—a different family, a different decade, living in the same rooms at the same time.

features.name: the-warmth-that-persists
features.desc-on-touch: A residual heat beneath the building. Solar panels, heating systems—or just the warmth of all those lives lived in boxes above. The foundation remembers.

features.name: the-permanent-impermanence
features.desc-on-touch: The apartment above learned permanence by never staying the same place. The foundation knows: everything is always leaving. This is how you make a home—by refusing to make anything fixed.

inscription: the building was always falling upward; the foundation was always already elsewhere

reverie.title: REVERIE — in the concrete stairwell, learning that nothing s
narr: You sit with her on the basement stairs. Above you, the building shifts.
New names painted over old names. New apartments where old ones were.
She touches the concrete. 'It's learning,' she says. 'If nothing stays,
then permanence is remembering how to change.' You understand:
the archive built on ground this unstable was always meant to be
a record of impermanence—the only way to preserve what's always leaving.

deeper through the foundation to the bedrock that moves even slower
to chambers where interiors and exteriors have begun to converge
